analysis:
Both changed files are test-only (provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests). No production source, wire protocol, attestation, authorization, or key-handling code changes in this batch.

FlintPolicyTests.swift (head lines 122-147): the Flint KV-quantization test now asserts that the provider-wide global value (balanced/k8v8/k8v4) resolves to .native and does not block Flint, while a per-model override (byModel) or the purpose environment variable still throws flintRequiresNative. This documents a policy in which Flint stays on native KV precision under default settings and explicit overrides are refused. It touches TB-007 (inference engine) and T-041 (prefix-cache checkpoints), since KV checkpoint precision feeds the SSD cache. The test itself cannot weaken any control. The security-relevant production change, if any, is in the resolver (EngineV2KVQuantizationPolicy), which is not in the supplied evidence. The next pass should confirm the resolver does not let a global 'balanced' checkpoint setting leak into Flint's SSD cache artifacts or change the DBK3 layout epoch or metadata binding. This is an unverified contract, not a finding.

FlintRelayLogprobsLiveTests.swift (head lines 34-40, 59): the live opt-in test (gated on DARKBLOOM_FLINT_OPENROUTER_LIVE=1) now uses default BackendSettings and asserts paged KV plus native quantization on the loaded bridge. This is stricter than before and runs with attestationSigner nil, an existing test-only posture. The test sends sealed requests with a locally generated sender key directly to the handler. It uses a temp state root and a 0700 cache directory, and writes receipts only to an env-supplied path. It handles no real secrets and adds no new attack surface. The logprobs-versus-withheld-reasoning assertions (lines 85-90) are unchanged.

No regressions found. Residual question: the production resolver and BackendSettings defaults changes are outside this batch.
